title: Streamline IO handoff and lightweight instrumentation runtime
creator: Rohan Desai
description: Background: Over the past year we've accumulated several hotspots in the runtime observability path: synchronous flushes from multiple instrumented subsystems, high contention in the global log/trace emitter, and unpredictable p99 latency spikes when garbage collection and I/O coincide. This ticket focuses on architectural and micro-optimizations to reduce CPU tail latency and memory churn in production.
goals: Reduce p99 trace/log emit CPU by at least 35% on serving nodes
Bound worst-case flush latency for telemetry to <50ms under steady load
Modularize instrumentation runtime so language bindings can opt into lightweight fastpath without full OTEL heavy deps
problem_statement: Current trace/log pipeline performs several synchronous handoffs and allocates per-span structs during flush paths. Producers may take locks when enqueuing, and the merge/serializer stage runs on request threads in some code paths causing high tail latency. Existing OTEL adapters pull in large transitive deps that block incremental upgrades and increase cold-start memory.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce a bounded MPSC handoff queue implemented with a lock-free ring buffer for fast producers; 2) Move serialization and network flush to a small pool of background workers with adaptive concurrency; 3) Implement a compact envelope format for internal telemetry to reduce allocations and allow zero-copy where possible; 4) Extract a lightweight instrumentation shim (redwood-instr-lite) that exposes minimal export points and can be wired into runtime hotpaths without full OTEL object graphs; 5) Add adaptive backpressure: when queue occupancy exceeds thresholds, telemetry producers switch to aggregated counters + sampled spans to limit pressure.
implementation_notes:
- Ring buffer will be bounded at configurable size per node (default 64k entries) with per-shard sizing for multi-core nodes.
- Background flusher threads use batch windows (max 4ms or 512 items) to improve throughput while respecting latency SLO.
- Compact envelope uses integer tag IDs + shared string table to reduce per-item overhead.
- redwood-instr-lite provides a tiny C API + Go/Java wrappers; it should be linkable without pulling full OTEL SDK.
- Migration plan: enable handoff in canary runtime, run benchmarks, then gradually toggle for low-latency services before global rollout.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag behind runtime-config: enable_ring_handoff=false by default.
2) Canary on dev/staging nodes for 48h with synthetic high telemetry load.
3) Gradual rollout to <10% of serving fleet for 72h with close monitoring.
4) If stable, ramp to 100% over one week.
5) Revert path: flip flag off and drain background queues.
risks_and_mitigation:
Race conditions in lock-free structures (mitigation: thorough property-based testing + fuzzing).
High memory due to large backlog (mitigation: bounded capacity + drop/sampling policy + alerting).
Compatibility issues with downstream exporters (mitigation: compatibility shim that can convert compact envelope to existing exporter formats).
Build complexity for redwood-instr-lite (mitigation: provide CI cross-build matrix and vendor-safe artifacts).
test_plan: Unit tests for ring buffer and flusher state machine, integration test that verifies no spans lost under load with controlled sampling, load test on perf cluster to validate targets, end-to-end functional test with tracing backends (Zipkin/OTLP) via compatibility shim.
monitoring_and_alerting:
New metrics: obs_handoff_queue_size, obs_handoff_drops, obs_flusher_batch_size, obs_flusher_latency_ms_p99.
Dashboards: per-node queue heatmap, background-flusher CPU utilization, per-service dropped telemetry rate.
Alert thresholds: queue_size > 80% for >1m, drops > 10/min, flusher_latency_p99 > 200ms.
